annotation.emotional_arc: A transition from quiet observation of twilight to a state of longing and dreamlike anticipation.

stanzas.loss_note: The translation of 'saj jaaye' (to adorn oneself / get ready) as 'come undone' in L4 completely reverses the literal meaning of the Hindi verb, changing the active preparation of the queen of dreams into a state of unraveling.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The darkness of night spreading across the landscape.
acceptable_visual_variants: A dark blue gradient sky rolling over hills like a soft fabric
A starry night sky slowly descending over a sleeping town
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: A bedsheet or blanket made of night
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: An illustrator might draw a literal giant fabric blanket floating down from the sky over a landscape, which looks comical rather than poetic.
metaphor_spans.tenor: the darkness of night covering the earth
metaphor_spans.vehicle: a blanket or bedsheet (चादर) being spread out
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a dark, starry sky gradually rolling over a twilight landscape like a soft, dark blue or black veil.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The personification of dreams or a beloved figure associated with sleep and dreaming.
acceptable_visual_variants: An ethereal female silhouette blending into a starry night sky
A peaceful sleeping face surrounded by soft, glowing dream-like swirls
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Drawing a literal queen with a crown sitting on a throne made of clouds might look too cartoonish or fantasy-like, losing the soft, romantic mood of the poem.
metaphor_spans.tenor: the onset of sleep, dreams, or a beloved dream-like figure
metaphor_spans.vehicle: a royal woman or queen (रानी) who rules or embodies dreams
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a soft, ethereal, semi-transparent female figure emerging from starlight or clouds, looking peaceful and dreamlike.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation 'come undone' completely reverses the meaning of the original Hindi verb 'saj jaaye' (सज जाए), which means to adorn oneself, get dressed up, or be beautifully prepared. This alters the imagery from a queen of dreams dressing up/adorning herself to her falling apart or coming undone.

annotation.theme: The transition from day to night as a catalyst for dreams and longing.

original_poem:
कहीं दूर जब दिन ढल जाए,  
सूर्य के संग जब छायाएँ मिल जाएं।  
जब रात की चादर बिछ जाए,  
तब सपनों की रानी सज जाए।
poem_title: Kahin Door Jab Din Dhal Jaaye
translated_poem:
When the day fades away in the distance,  
When shadows meet with the setting sun.  
When the blanket of night is spread wide,  
Then the queen of dreams will come undone.
